source_check: Checked against the full texts read in the blind round (PMC4158030, PMC4459504, PMC7450360; Liu text saved in the reader's scratch folder). No new browser tab was needed.

results.note: Five reports, four cohorts (three reports from two US, two from two Norwegian), n 447-1311, school or community based: all as stated. The source says three were published 'within the past 3 years'; 'before the search' is a gloss.

Table 2A weighted: 0.57 (0.06); abuse or dependence symptoms 0.36 (0.07); other substance outcomes also significant (Results, 1st paragraph). 'Drinking by 14' means a drink without parental permission by the age-14 assessment (mean 14.8).
Table 2A, all discordant pairs: 0.21 (0.09), z 2.33; 0.24 (0.11), z 2.18. Results, 2nd paragraph, reports within-pair effects significant at p<0.05.
MZ: 0.22 (0.10), z 2.2; 0.17 (0.14), z 1.21, two-sided p about 0.22. Printed p-values track the normal density. 486 MZ pairs x 20% discordance = 97.2: roughly 97 holds, as an estimate.

Table 2B, all discordant pairs: 0.37 (0.13), z 2.85, p about 0.004; 0.29 (0.15), z 1.93, p about 0.053, borderline but not significant. Intoxication was 'by FU1' (mean age 14.8). Role 'qualifies' fits.

results.corrected_extracted: Across sources, co-use among people who use cocaine varied widely: simultaneous alcohol 24% to 98%, simultaneous cannabis 12% to 76%, concurrent alcohol 37% to 96%, concurrent cannabis 43% to 94% (ranges as stated in the text; three of them do not match the table, whose values run 23.5% to 87%, 9.3% to 76.5% and 34.9% to 96.5%; study card reporting issue).
results.corrected_locator: 3. Results › 3.1.1. Review of studies including PSU prevalence, 1st paragraph; Table 1, Polysubstance use rate column
results.note: All numbers verified (Table 1 lows WTW 23.5 and 9.3, Vanek 34.9; highs Licht 87, Barrett 2005 76.5, Grant & Harford 96.5). Only the locator changes: the table values are in Table 1, not 3.1.1.

results.corrected_extracted: Definitions differed: simultaneous use meant use at the same time or within a couple of hours, co-administration in a session, co-use at first cocaine use, using alcohol or cannabis to come down from a cocaine high, or using them together with cocaine and a prescription drug in the past 12 months (Rx study); concurrent use meant both substances within 30 days, 6 months, a year or a lifetime, both positive in one urine test, or an unstated window (one source); several rates were calculated by the authors from the articles' data.
results.note: Everything stated is correct (3.1.1, 2nd paragraph; Table 1 Measure; Discussion, 1st paragraph: Booth, Hedden, Vanek). The list left out two Table 1 definitions: Rx's 12-month 'together' and Schwingel's unspecified window.
